glosses: A proverb or proverbial expression, common saying; a frequently used word or phrase.
A characteristic word or expression; a word or phrase associated with a person or group.

examples.text: Illustrious unfortunates attract a wider sympathy, not because their griefs are more intense, but because, being set on lofty pedestals, they the better serve mankind as instances and bywords of calamity.
examples.ref: 1846, Nathaniel Hawthorne, “The Christmas Banquet”, in Mosses from an Old Manse:

glosses: Someone or something that stands as an example (i.e. metonymically) for something else, by having some of that something's characteristic traits.

examples.text: He hath made me also a byword of the people […]
examples.ref: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Job 17:6:

examples.text: "I know you and Harry are inseparable. Surely for that reason, if for none other, you should not have made his sister's name a by-word."
